newsitem.title: FRANCE: European anglers protest against winged rivals.
newsitem.headline: European anglers protest against winged rivals.

text.p: Thousands of European anglers demonstrated in France on Saturday against protection of their winged rivals -- proliferating cormorants which they accuse of emptying rivers of fish.

Some 5,000 protesters from France, Germany, Switzerland and Austria marched through the eastern French city of Strasbourg, headquarters of the European Parliament, to demand the repeal of a 17-year-old European Union directive protecting the birds.

They say cormorants, which each gobble up half-a-kilo (a pound) of fish a day, have multiplied out of control in northern Europe over the past 15 years. Their numbers have increased to 650,000 from 50,000 and are growing by 20 percent a year.
"They have virtually emptied the Rhine river of white fish. We are heading for an ecological disaster," said Marcel Carabin of the anglers federation in the Strasbourg region.
Anglers fear cormorants will also ruin efforts to re-introduce salmon, sea-trout and eels in the Rhine.
Environmentalists say the fish population is dwindling, largely because of industrial contamination, but many admit cormorants are contributing.
Rather than allowing the birds to be hunted, they propose re-introducing birds of prey into the cormorants' breeding grounds to cut their reproduction rate.
